summary: Split-flap tiles (a Solari board): a fixed number of tiles that, when the text they show changes, flip forward through a drum of characters (or whole words) to the new ones, with the mechanical half-flap fold, rippling across the tiles and down the rows.

text.doc: A fixed text, one tile per character, flipping in from blank when the document appears (characters must be on the drum; lower case is shown upper case). For text that changes, pass code and tiles instead

code.doc: The drum index each tile shows now, as an expression of i (the tile, from 0) and r (the row, from 0): "arrayGet(@chars, @row * 5 + i)", or a digit of the clock "27 + floor(@hhmm / pow(10, 3 - i)) % 10". When it changes, set prev to the old index and restart since

prev.doc: The drum index each tile showed before the change, an expression of i and r (default 0, the drum's first glyph: blank), so the tiles flip forward from prev to code

since.doc: Seconds since the change (default animationTime(): the tiles flip in when the document appears). A board that changes every 9 s passes "animationTime() % 9"; a clock that flips on the minute "continuousSec() % 60"

tiles.doc: How many tiles a row has (with code; text gives its length). May be an expression

rows.doc: How many rows of tiles: r runs from 0 to rows - 1, each row tileHeight + rowGap below the last

drum.doc: The glyphs on the drum, in flip order, the first one blank. Indices (code, prev) count glyphs on this string

glyphWidth.doc: Characters per glyph: 1 for letters, more for word flaps (a drum of equal-width words, padded with spaces: "        ON TIME BOARDINGDELAYED " with glyphWidth 8)

align.doc: Where the glyph sits on its tile: centred (letters) or from the start, inset by inset x tileHeight (words)

inset.doc: With align start: the glyph's left inset, as a fraction of tileHeight

tileHeight.doc: A tile's height in dp; the glyph is textSize x this

textSize.doc: Glyph size as a fraction of tileHeight (may be an expression)

bold.doc: Thicken the glyphs with a stroke (canvas text has no font weight)

delay.doc: Seconds from the change to the first tile's first flap

ripple.doc: Extra delay per tile along a row, in seconds

rowRipple.doc: Extra delay per row, in seconds

jitter.doc: Up to this many seconds of hashed per-tile delay, so the flurry looks mechanical; 0 for lockstep

tileX.doc: A tile's x in dp, an expression of i (default i x (tileWidth + gap)): for groups of tiles with wider gaps between fields, read from an array

tileY.doc: Extra y in dp for a tile, an expression of i (default 0): a second line of tiles in the same row

rowPitch.doc: Distance from one row's top to the next in dp (default tileHeight + rowGap)

x.doc: With fill: the first tile's left in dp inside the canvas

y.doc: With fill: the first row's top in dp inside the canvas

fill.doc: Fill the space it is given (fillMaxSize) and draw at x, y instead of sizing itself to the tiles: for a board that lays tiles out itself with expressions

width.doc: Width in dp when the size cannot be computed from tiles (tiles or tileX an expression)

height.doc: Height in dp when the size cannot be computed from rows

label.doc: What a screen reader says (default text)

tileColor.doc: The tile, behind the flap (default track: a mid grey that stands off the page and carries onSurface glyphs at 8:1 or more in light and dark)

flapColor.doc: The flap's face (the top half at rest); a shade lighter than tileColor gives the classic two-tone tile

shadeColor.doc: The shadow on the flap as it turns edge-on (faded by paint alpha)

pitfalls: A real flap only moves forward: from prev to code it shows every glyph in between, (code - prev) mod the drum size steps at speed flaps a second, so a long jump takes longer. Order the drum so frequent changes are short
SplitFlap does not remember what it showed: when code changes, pass the old index as prev and restart since (a board cycling through an array passes the previous entry and animationTime() % period)
Inside code, prev and tileX, i is the tile and r the row (the component's loop indices); don't name document variables i or r
The tiles redraw every frame while since moves (about 25 draw operations a tile): a 26 x 9 board is around 6 000 operations a frame. Fine for a board or a kiosk, heavy for a small widget
Mono shows code as it is, with no flip and no shading: outlined tiles and a split cut through them
